# From Poverty to Power

> > Oxfam's platform for feminist development research, grassroots activism, and evidence-based advocacy addressing poverty, inequality, and social change in the Global South.

From Poverty to Power is Oxfam's flagship blog and research platform featuring analysis from leading development scholars like Naila Kabeer and Duncan Green. It covers feminist development, climate resilience, land rights, activism, and economic justice through both research articles and on-the-ground reporting from regions including Bangladesh, Kenya, and South Sudan.

## Key Topics

- Feminist development
- Gender equality
- Land and water rights
- Climate resilience
- Women empowerment
- Activism and civic engagement
- Economic justice
- Community-led development
- Food security
- Trade policy and industrial development
- Decolonisation in development work
- Refugee stories and displacement
- Aid effectiveness
- Global South perspectives
- Humanitarian response

## Core Resources

- [From Poverty to Power](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk): Homepage for Oxfam's development & activism platform featuring Naila Kabeer research.
- [Women in the Global South know exactly how to support their own communities – so why don't we get behind them?](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/womens-rights-fund): Oxfam Women's Rights Fund promoting grassroots women-led organizations.

## Feminist Development & Gender

- [Multiple pathways to personhood: How Bangladeshi women managed to renegotiate patriarchy](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/multiple-pathways-to-personhood-how-bangladeshi-women-managed-to-renegotiate-patriarchy): Analysis of women's agency & patriarchy negotiation in Bangladesh by Naila Kabeer.
- [Want feminist development that builds climate resilience? Then we have to talk about land and water rights](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/want-feminist-development-that-builds-climate-resilience-then-we-have-to-talk-about-land-and-water-rights): Feminist perspective on land/water rights & climate resilience by Oxfam researchers.
- [The financing for development conference let us down: now the fight for feminist economic justice continues](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/the-financing-for-development-conference-let-us-down-now-the-fight-for-feminist-economic-justice-continues): Feminist critique of FFD4 conference & global South debt & care work issues.

## Activism & Social Change

- [The first 6 months of LSE's new Activism, Influence and Change programme – a report back + where next](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/the-first-6-months-of-lses-new-activism-influence-and-change-programme-a-report-back-where-next): LSE programme progress report on activism & civil society advocacy training.
- [From Salaamz to the Streets: Three Lessons from Kenya's June 2024 Protests](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/from-salaamz-to-the-streets-three-lessons-from-kenyas-june-2024-protests): Analysis of Kenya's 2024 youth protests & civic activism lessons.
- [Jobs were moved – but not power: the failings of 'decolonisation'](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/jobs-were-moved-but-not-power-the-failings-of-decolonisation): Critical analysis of decolonisation failures in NGO sector power structures.

## Development Policy & Economics

- [The old neoliberal consensus on trade and developing countries is dying… so what will replace it?](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/the-old-neoliberal-consensus-trade-dying): Duncan Green on WTO reform & industrial policy for developing countries.
- [Ethical storytelling can help us fight back after the aid cuts](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/ethical-storytelling-can-help-us-fight-back-after-the-aid-cuts): NGO communications strategy for equitable storytelling & advocacy amid aid cuts.

## Humanitarian & Climate Crisis

- [The world is seeing more extreme heat – so why don't we plan for it like other humanitarian disasters?](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/the-world-is-seeing-more-extreme-heat-so-why-dont-we-plan-for-it-like-other-humanitarian-disasters): Humanitarian perspective on extreme heat preparedness in Bangladesh & South Sudan.
- [School-age children aren't getting the food they need in emergencies – why have they been forgotten?](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/school-age-food-emergencies-forgotten): Analysis of child nutrition gaps in humanitarian emergencies in Nigeria.

## Voices & Stories

- ['I started writing poetry because I had no other way to speak': interview with poet and refugee Peter Kidi](https://frompoverty.oxfam.org.uk/i-started-writing-poetry-because-i-had-no-other-way-to-speak-interview-with-poet-and-refugee-peter-kidi): Interview with South Sudanese refugee poet Peter Kidi from Kakuma camp.
